Subject: Proposed DPA amendment - runtime analytics retention & partner processors

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Helios' data team is excited about Redwood's latency and batch features. Our legal team circulated a small DPA amendment this morning to cover two items they need for procurement sign-off:

1) Explicit language that runtime inference telemetry (latency histograms and anonymized error rates) will be retained for no more than 90 days, and will not be used to train models.
2) A carveout that allows Helios to pre-approve a short list of analytics subprocessors (e.g., MetricsCorp) that will only receive aggregated telemetry, not inference payloads.

I've attached Helios_DPA_Amendment_v3.pdf that redlines our standard DPA. Can your team confirm Product and Security sign-off? Procurement is hoping to close the PO by the end of next week.

Appreciate a quick path here — happy to hop on a call.

Best,
Tanya Ramesh
Head of Procurement, Helios Analytics

Thanks Tanya — I got the attachment and looped in Security (Olga) and Product (Aditya + Marcus) for technical/operational feasibility.

Quick read: both asks seem reasonable but there are details we need to confirm before sign-off:
- Retention: 90 days is fine for aggregated latency metrics. We need to confirm whether Helios expects raw KV cache traces or only aggregated percentiles/histograms.
- Training language: our standard DPA already disallows derivative model training on customer payloads, but Product needs explicit wording about "telemetry-only" artifacts.
- Subprocessor carveout: we can agree to an allowlist model for analytics partners provided they only receive anonymized, aggregated telemetry and sign a data-limited subprocessor addendum. We may need to add an approval/maintenance process for the allowlist.

Olga / Aditya / Marcus — please advise on the operational constraints and suggested wording. If this is all green we can propose redline_helios_v4.docx to legal and send back to Tanya this week.

Sofia

On Tue, Oct 14, 2025 at 10:04 AM Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.inference.com> wrote:
> Olga / Aditya / Marcus — please advise on the operational constraints and suggested wording.

Quick notes from Security:
- 90 days retention for aggregated telemetry (latency percentiles, error rates) is acceptable. Must ensure no request/response payload (inputs/outputs) ever leaves the runtime for analytics partners.
- "Not used to train models" is strong language; we prefer "not used to train customer-facing models or derivatives thereof without explicit customer consent". That covers internal infra improvements while protecting customer data.
- For subprocessors: adopt a two-step: (1) allowlist of named processors in the DPA exhibit; (2) each new processor triggers a notification + 30-day review where the customer can object. This balances Helios' procurement needs with our security posture.

Operational constraints for Product:
- Marcus: to produce only aggregated percentiles we need to enable a telemetry aggregation pipeline and a configuration knob per customer. That work is on the roadmap Q1 2026 unless we prioritize as an exception.
- Aditya: if Helios requires immediate integration with MetricsCorp we can implement an anonymized export, but it will add ~3-4 weeks to onboarding and requires a short-term waiver for telemetry export auditing.

Recommendation: propose redline language that: (a) limits telemetry to aggregated latency/error metrics retained 90 days; (b) clarifies the non-training clause to include explicit consent; (c) includes an allowlist and 30-day objection window. We'll need a brief SOC/ops checklist attached for procurement.

Olga Petrov
Head of Security Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: sofia_ivanova <sofia@redwood.inference.com>

Date: Thu, 16 Oct 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed DPA amendment - runtime analytics retention & partner processors

Hi Tanya — thanks for the patience. We've reviewed Helios' amendment and prepared a proposed redline and an operations checklist. Summary of our positions: 

1) Retention & telemetry scope: Redwood agrees to retain aggregated runtime telemetry (latency percentiles, success/error rates, anonymized sampling counts) for a maximum of 90 days. We confirm that no raw request/response payloads or KV cache dumps will be exported as telemetry.

2) Training prohibition: We will add the following clarified clause — "Redwood will not use customer request or response payloads, nor telemetry derived from raw payloads, to train customer-facing or production models without explicit written consent from the customer." This permits internal infrastructure tuning on aggregated signals while protecting Helios' data.

3) Subprocessor allowlist: We can include an exhibit with pre-approved analytics subprocessors (MetricsCorp as requested). New subprocessors will be added via a notification and 30-day review window during which the customer may object and request additional controls. Each subprocessor must sign a data-limited subprocessor addendum before receiving any exported telemetry.

Next steps: we've attached our redline_helios_v4.docx and a short SOC/ops checklist. If Helios legal is OK with the 30-day add/remove process and the clarified training clause, we can route this to procurement and finalize the PO. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute call with Olga and Aditya to walk the legal team through the operational controls.
